Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Aurora Renewables Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants may register for the Q&A by pressing star then one on their touchtone phone. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aurora Renewables' results for the third quarter. Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Financial Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Sophia Chen, Chief Technology Officer; and Liam Ortiz, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by our continued focus on innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability. We are seeing strong demand for our renewable energy solutions across all markets.

Here are six key highlights from the quarter:

First, on our operating capacity and generation output. We ended the quarter with a total nameplate capacity of 12.8 gigawatts, reflecting a 28 percent year-over-year increase from 10 gigawatts at the end of Q3 last year. This expansion came mainly from bringing three major projects into commercial operation: the 450-megawatt Desert Sunlight Extension solar-plus-storage facility in California's Mojave Desert, which includes 200 megawatt-hours of Tesla Megapack battery energy storage systems; the 320-megawatt onshore wind farm in the U.S. Midwest's Iowa Dakotas region equipped with Vestas V150-4.2-megawatt turbines; and the initial 150-megawatt phase of our 600-megawatt Moray East offshore wind project off Scotland's coast, using Siemens Gamesa SG 14-222 double-digit direct-drive turbines designed for low-wind-speed environments. By technology, solar makes up 42 percent of our portfolio at 5.4 gigawatts, up 35 percent year-over-year with bifacial PERC modules from LONGi and Trina Solar pushing our average DC/AC ratio to 1.35 from 1.25. Wind represents 48 percent or 6.1 gigawatts, with offshore at 22 percent of that for superior capacity factors, and battery storage at 10 percent or 1.3 gigawatts and 4.2 gigawatt-hours, surging 150 percent year-over-year as we pair renewables with dispatchable storage to counter grid curtailment. Regionally, North America holds 68 percent or 8.7 gigawatts, boosted by the Inflation Reduction Act's production tax credit and investment tax credit extensions that grew our U.S. pipeline to 32 gigawatts; Europe, Middle East, and Africa account for 24 percent or 3.1 gigawatts with UK Contracts for Difference auctions and German EEG feed-in tariffs; and Asia-Pacific is at 8 percent or 1 gigawatt, targeting Australia's National Electricity Market with 10-year power purchase agreements at AUD 75 per megawatt-hour with Origin Energy. On generation, we produced 7.2 terawatt-hours in the quarter, up 18 percent from 6.1 terawatt-hours last year, even with below-average sunlight in the U.S. Southwest—15 percent fewer peak sun hours due to Saharan dust—while our fleet-wide capacity factor rose to 25.8 percent, gaining 120 basis points through proactive operations and maintenance. Solar output was 2.9 terawatt-hours at 24.5 percent capacity factor, edging out competitors with Nextracker systems at 60-degree tilts; onshore wind delivered 2.8 terawatt-hours at 32.1 percent with AI-driven wake steering cutting yaw losses by 8 percent; offshore wind added 1.1 terawatt-hours at 42.3 percent on 11.5 meters-per-second winds; and storage contributed 0.4 terawatt-hours of firming and arbitrage at 92 percent round-trip efficiency using our vanadium redox flow technology with Invinity Energy Systems. We saw a 5 percent quarter-over-quarter utilization boost from grid upgrades, resolving 95 percent of U.S. interconnection backlogs after FERC Order 2023, with forced outages down 12 percent to 1.2 percent via GE Vernova's Predix analytics, though ERCOT curtailment hit 2 percent, addressed by 500 megawatts in virtual power plant contracts. This sets us up with a 45-gigawatt pipeline—60 percent solar-plus-storage hybrids—for 20 percent compound annual growth in capacity through 2027, levelized cost of energy at $25 per megawatt-hour for solar, and 85 percent PPA coverage at $45 blended to shield from volatility.

Second, our overall performance highlights and key achievements. This quarter marked exceptional results across our integrated clean energy platform, including utility-scale solar PV, onshore and offshore wind, battery storage, and green hydrogen pilots, amid tailwinds like the IRA tax credits, EU REPowerEU, and renewables' levelized cost of energy under $30 per megawatt-hour in prime areas per BloombergNEF. Revenue jumped 48 percent year-over-year to $1.47 billion, powered by 62 percent growth in engineering, procurement, and construction and full ramp-up of our 2.5-gigawatt Texas solar module plant; nine-month revenue hit $4.2 billion, on pace for $6.0 to $6.3 billion full-year, up 42 percent. Adjusted EBITDA rose 55 percent to $428 million with margins at 29.1 percent, up 320 basis points from supply chain gains and premium power purchase agreements; our 18-gigawatt backlog across 45 projects values at over $25 billion through 2030. Net income to shareholders was $210 million or $0.78 per diluted share, up from $0.52, aided by $45 million IRA investment tax credit on SunForge Solar Farm; free cash flow reached $320 million, funding $150 million share buybacks and a 12 percent dividend increase to $0.25 per share. Balance sheet strong with net debt-to-EBITDA at 1.8 times and $2.1 billion liquidity. Operationally, we added 1.8 gigawatts, totaling 12.4 gigawatts operating, up 35 percent: 850-megawatt SunForge in Imperial Valley with TOPCon modules at 24.8 percent efficiency and 28.5 percent capacity factor via Enphase microinverters, under 15-year PPA at $42 per megawatt-hour with Southern California Edison; 1.2-gigawatt North Sea Breeze offshore with Siemens Gamesa 15-megawatt turbines at 52 percent capacity factor; 450 megawatt-hours AuroraFlow storage in a 200-megawatt/800-megawatt-hour Texas hybrid boosting revenue 15 percent in ERCOT ancillary markets. We avoided 8.2 million metric tons of CO2 equivalent, like removing 1.8 million cars, with 99.7 percent uptime via AuroraAI maintenance. North America at 52 percent revenue with IRA-fueled 1.1-gigawatt queue additions; Europe 28 percent with €1.2 billion Contracts for Difference; APAC 20 percent with 75 percent India solar growth and 300-megawatt New South Wales storage. Innovation includes heterojunction cells at 26.2 percent efficiency for $20 per megawatt-hour levelized cost of energy by 2026 and 100-megawatt Rotterdam electrolyzer for steel decarbonization. We closed $850 million WindTech acquisition adding 2 gigawatts onshore IP and issued $5 billion green bonds at 4.2 percent for 4 gigawatts hybrids. FY24 revenue to top end at $6.3 billion, 2025 guidance $8.0-8.5 billion on $1.5 trillion global capex.

Third, PPA pricing trends and contract extensions. Our 8.2-gigawatt operating assets—mostly solar PV, onshore wind, and hybrids—are 95 percent contracted through 2030 for stability. Pricing continued downward from module costs at $0.22 per watt-peak for TOPCon bifacials and stabilized turbine OEMs, with global unsubsidized solar PPAs at $24 per megawatt-hour, down 18 percent year-over-year and 42 percent from 2021 peaks per LevelTen and Aurora Energy Research; wind at $26 per megawatt-hour, down 15 percent. In the U.S., 65 percent of pipeline, CAISO/ERCOT hybrids averaged $22 per megawatt-hour boosted 20-25 percent by IRA pass-throughs; MISO/PJM at $28 with tolled storage fees. Europe at €32 per megawatt-hour ($35 equivalent), up 5 percent on Contracts for Difference like UK AR6 at £42 strike; emerging markets like Australia AUD 35 ($23) and India INR 2.5 per kilowatt-hour ($30). Levelized cost of energy compression to $25-30 solar, $28-35 wind per NREL, tempered by 3.2 percent inflation and O&M like robotic cleaners; Q4 stabilizing at $23-25. Extensions added $1.2 billion to 10-year EBITDA, up 30 percent, with 1.8 gigawatts into 20-plus-year terms at 12-18 percent uplifts: 350-megawatt Desert Sun with APS to Southern California Edison at $32 fixed plus 2 percent CPI and $3 storage adder; Texas Panhandle wind repower with perovskite tandems extending Exelon PPA at $29 with RECs. 'PPA 2.0' hybrids: 70 percent fixed, 20 percent capacity, 10 percent merchant as in 500-megawatt Microsoft deal. Battery mandates in 80 percent new PPAs lift prices 15 percent; geographic focus on hyperscalers; hedging 50 percent expiries. Extensions now 65 percent backlog support 12-15 percent FY25 revenue growth; raised FY24 midpoint $50 million.

Fourth, development pipeline additions and project milestones. Our pipeline hit 52.3 gigawatts, up 28 percent year-over-year, capturing decarbonization, data centers, and reshoring via AI site screening on 15 million U.S. acres. Q3 added 14.2 gigawatts for 30-gigawatt five-year target: 6.8 gigawatts solar with 23.5 percent TOPCon in Arizona Maricopa; 4.1 gigawatts onshore wind like 1.2-gigawatt Oklahoma with GE Vernova 5.X-16; 2.5 gigawatts/8.2 gigawatt-hours BESS with LFP from CATL/Fluence including 1.1 gigawatts California; 0.8 gigawatts green hydrogen/floating solar like 400-megawatt DOE hubs and 200-megawatt Southeast pilots. U.S. 65 percent with $2.4 billion tax credits; Europe 20 percent with 1.8 gigawatts German/Spanish; APAC 15 percent Australia. Milestones de-risked 8.7 gigawatts: U.S. 800-megawatt Desert Bloom hybrid NTP with NV Energy/$450 million JPMorgan, $22 levelized cost of energy; 650-megawatt Plainswind FERC/PPA Microsoft $35; 300-megawatt ERCOT BESS queued #14. Europe: 500-megawatt Dutch offshore permitting; 400-megawatt Iberica PPA Iberdrola €25. Global: Air Products 100-megawatt hydrogen MOU; 150-megawatt Florida floating LOI. 85 percent late-stage with PPAs/LOIs, queue 1.5 years; 20-gigawatt FY25 additions.

Fifth, revenue and earnings growth analysis. Q3 revenue $1.28 billion, up 48 percent year-over-year and 12 percent sequential, nine-months $3.65 billion toward $5.1-5.3 billion full-year, 52 percent over 2023. Solar 42 percent/$538 million up 62 percent on 4.2-gigawatt PPAs/IRA 45X $145 million; wind 28 percent/$358 million up 39 percent on 55 percent capacity factors/AI yaw; storage 22 percent/$282 million up 71 percent on 1.5 gigawatt-hours/95 percent efficiency hyperscaler deals; EPC/O&M 8 percent/$102 million up 25 percent. North America 61 percent/$781 million 55 percent growth IRA $320 million; Europe 24 percent/$307 million 42 percent REPowerEU; APAC 12 percent/$154 million 35 percent hydrogen offset. EBITDA $285 million up 67 percent, 22.3 percent margins; gross 28.4 percent from gigafactory/polysilicon $8.5/kilogram; net $162 million/$0.78 EPS 12.7 percent margin. Levelized cost of energy $28 solar; 85 percent contracted; OpEx 18 percent R&D perovskites; $450 million buyback/$1.2 billion cash. Capex $750 million BESS/electrolyzer; Q4 $1.4-1.5 billion, FY25 $7.2-7.8 billion 25 percent-plus margins.

Sixth, new PPAs secured and average pricing. We secured 1.4 gigawatts across eight projects, best since Q1 2022, lifting contracted backlog to 12.3 gigawatts up 28 percent, 17-year average life from 18-gigawatt pipeline 70 percent shovel-ready. Wins: 450-megawatt Desert Bloom solar-plus-storage Southern California Edison; 650 megawatts Microsoft/Google wind-solar 15-year CPI-escalated; 300-megawatt Italy floating Enel. Positions 2.1 gigawatts 2025 commission tax equity-funded. Average $32 per megawatt-hour levelized cost of energy equivalent, flat QoQ up 5 percent YoY vs. LevelTen $26 U.S. solar. Premium from 60 percent storage 15-20 percent uplift like $38 base/$12 ERCOT; regional $35-42 ERCOT/$30 CAISO/$28 PJM/€45 Europe; 55 percent utility/45 percent corporate 18-20 years 2-3 percent escalators. Queue-first 85 percent energized; 5 gigawatts modules banked. 4.5-gigawatt 2025 pipeline $31-34; 12-14 percent levered IRRs.

Now, I will turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. We are very pleased with our financial performance in Q3. Revenue was $1.47 billion, a 48 percent increase year-over-year. This increase was driven by higher project commissioning and energy sales. Gross margin was 29.1 percent, reflecting improved cost management and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $800 million, primarily due to increased investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $210 million, or $0.78 per share. We ended the quarter with $2.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee for an update on our project pipeline.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Marcus. Our project pipeline continues to grow, with 52.3 gigawatts of projects under development. We are making good progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters. We are also actively exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

Next, Dr. Chen will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Sophia Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. We are committed to developing and deploying innovative technologies that improve the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy systems. We are making significant progress on our research and development efforts, including advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. We believe that these technologies will play a critical role in accelerating the transition to a clean energy future. The development of AuroraFlow is expected to have a 15 percent uplift in revenue capture on our future projects.

And now, Liam Ortiz will provide an update on our sustainability efforts.

Liam Ortiz:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We are committed to operating our business in a sustainable manner and minimizing our environmental impact. We have set ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that promote sustainability. We believe that sustainability is not only the right thing to do but also makes good business sense. Our portfolio avoided 8.2 million metric tons of CO2 equivalent this quarter, and we maintained 99.7 percent asset uptime.

I'll now turn the call back to Elena for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Liam. In closing, we are confident that Aurora Renewables is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for the Q&A session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Green Capital. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Can you provide more details on the regulatory environment for renewable energy projects in your key markets?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, John. The regulatory landscape remains supportive overall. In the U.S., the Inflation Reduction Act's PTC and ITC extensions, plus transferability, have supercharged our North American growth, accelerating pipelines and unlocking billions in credits. FERC Order 2023 has cleared much of the interconnection backlog, with 95 percent resolved for us. Europe's REPowerEU and UK Contracts for Difference auctions are driving offshore and solar, while Germany's EEG and Spain's RD 565/2023 frameworks aid permitting. In APAC, Australia's Capacity Investment Scheme and India's PLI incentives bolster storage and solar. We're navigating risks like permitting delays with a dedicated team, but tailwinds dominate as grids prioritize renewables.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with EcoInvest. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
How is the company addressing the challenges of energy storage integration with your renewable energy projects?

Dr. Sophia Chen:
Great question, Sarah. Storage integration is core to our hybrids, with over 60 percent of new PPAs including 2-4 hour BESS for duck curve mitigation and arbitrage. Our AuroraFlow systems, using LFP from CATL and Fluence JV, hit 95 percent round-trip efficiency with proprietary AI dispatch optimizing for ERCOT ancillary services and CAISO peaks—unlocking 15 percent higher capture prices. We've deployed 1.3 gigawatts/4.2 gigawatt-hours operating, including 450 megawatt-hours this quarter, with black-start NERC certification and VPP contracts mitigating curtailment. Next-gen vanadium flow and long-duration pilots address 6-gigawatt shortfalls like AEMO's, positioning us for frequency response revenue.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with RenewTech Partners. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
What are your expectations for the long-term growth of the renewable energy market?

Elena Vasquez:
Mike, we're bullish. IEA forecasts $1.5-1.7 trillion annual clean tech capex to Net Zero 2050, with renewables outpacing fossils in new builds. U.S. hyperscaler load growth at 15-20 percent CAGR, Europe's net-zero post-Ukraine, and global LCOE under $30 per megawatt-hour fuel 20 percent-plus industry CAGR. Our 52-gigawatt pipeline, 85 percent contracted at stable pricing, vertical integration, and M&A like WindTech target 42 percent revenue CAGR to 2026, with levered IRRs 12-14 percent. We're shaping the $1.7 trillion market.

Operator:
Instructions for the Q&A. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Aurora Renewables. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
